instructions: Yen is a transparency platform for community funds in India. Correctness of money, permissions and the tamper-evident event log matters more than style. TypeScript monorepo (pnpm, Turborepo, Biome, Vitest), Postgres, Solidity/Foundry. Money is integer paise. Prefer a few high-signal comments over many nitpicks.

rules.rule: Money amounts must be integer paise using the Paise branded type from @yen/shared. Flag floating-point arithmetic, parseFloat, or plain number/string used for amounts.
Never UPDATE or DELETE rows in fund_events or Konto ledger tables. Event writes must go through appendEvent only.
Any code that posts to the ledger must append the matching event in the same database transaction. Flag ledger writes and event appends in separate transactions.
Every API route that reads or changes fund data must authorize through can() and shape output through redact(). Flag routes that query fund data directly and return it.
Event payloads, Merkle leaves, logs, error reports and on-chain data must not contain phone numbers, names, UPI IDs, bank account numbers or OTPs. Use pseudonymous IDs.
Money-affecting POST handlers, webhook consumers and background jobs must be idempotent (idempotency key, unique constraint, or dedupe key) and safe to retry or replay.
External input (HTTP bodies, webhooks, partner payloads, env vars, file uploads) must be validated with zod at the boundary. Flag unchecked casts of external data and any use of any.

Database migrations must be forward-only, safe on tables with data (no long locks, no destructive drops without a prior release), and must not touch immutable event or ledger tables except to add constraints.
User-facing strings must be translatable (EN and HI) and avoid jargon such as hash, block, ledger, wallet, on-chain. Use plain words like record, proof, account book.
Changes to money, permission, hashing or approval logic must include tests that would fail if the behavior broke. Flag such changes with no test changes.

Design rationale that claims industry practice or security properties must cite a source in docs/REFERENCES.md; flag unsourced “industry standard” or “best practice” claims in ADRs, READMEs and PR descriptions for design changes.
